{{Short description|Israeli physicist (born 1960)}}
'''Adiel (Ady) Stern''' ({{Langx|he|עדי שטרן}}; born 1960) is an Israeli [[physicist]].

Ady Stern is a professor at the Condensed Matter Physics Department at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] and a theoretical physicist focused on the ways quantum theory manifests in electronic systems. He is best known for his research on the theoretical aspects of the fractional quantum Hall effect<ref>{{cite news |date=March 2, 2002 |title=Fractional quantum Hall effects |url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/indepth/734 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071027041700/http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/indepth/734 |archivedate=October 27, 2007 |accessdate=2011-08-29 |publisher=PhysicsWorld.com}}</ref> and the existence of quasiparticles with one-quarter the charge of an electron.<ref>[http://www.eetimes.com/document.asp?doc_id=1251090 Researchers claim to find particles with quarter-electron charge]</ref> In his scientific work, Stern emphasizes finding clear physical interpretations for complex phenomena, while his passion for popularizing science is reflected in his hobby of science communication.

In 2025 he won the IOP's [[Simon Memorial Prize]]: Low Temperature Group for his original and influential theoretical work on the quantum Hall effect, quantum statistics of emerging quasi-particles, topological order and decoherence in condensed matter systems at low temperatures.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Simon Memorial Prize: Low Temperature Group {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/physics-community/special-interest-groups/low-temperature-group/simon-memorial-prize |access-date=2025-05-06 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Ady was born and raised in [[Beersheba]], and presently lives in [[Tel Aviv|Tel-Aviv]]. he studied in [[Tel Aviv University|Tel-Aviv University]] for a B.Sc. in Mathematics, Computer Science and Physics, and for a Ph.D. in Physics. Following his Ph.D. he spent three years as a Junior Fellow at the [[Harvard University|Harvard]] Society of Fellows, and at the end of these three years he joined the Weizmann Institute as a faculty member.<ref>{{Cite web |website=Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities |title=Ady Stern |url=https://www.academy.ac.il/SystemFiles/23702.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240611034814/https://www.academy.ac.il/SystemFiles/23702.pdf |archive-date=11 June 2024}}</ref>
